purpose: Maintain consistent translation of important Bhagavad Gita spiritual and philosophical terminology across all target languages.
rules: Translate concepts according to their meaning in the supplied Telugu source.
Do not replace a concept with an unrelated modern or colloquial word merely because it is easier to understand.
Use the same established target-language terminology consistently throughout the complete 100-entry translation.
If a target language commonly retains a Sanskrit spiritual term, the established Sanskrit-derived term may be retained.
Do not translate the Sanskrit shloka itself.
Do not add explanations that are not present in the source.
Do not remove explanations that are present in the source.
When a term has multiple possible translations, prefer the translation that preserves the spiritual/philosophical meaning of the source.
Terminology consistency must be maintained within each language.

coreTerms.instruction: Translate according to the spiritual meaning of Atman or the Self in the source context.
Translate according to the context of the source. Do not unnecessarily change between personal and impersonal meanings.
Preserve the philosophical meaning of dharma. Do not reduce it automatically to merely religion, law, or morality.
Use the context of the source to determine whether karma refers to action, deed, or the broader philosophical concept of karma.
Preserve the spiritual/philosophical meaning of yoga. Do not automatically interpret it as physical exercise.
Preserve the meaning of devotional relationship with the Divine.
Preserve the spiritual and philosophical sense of knowledge rather than merely academic information.
Preserve the spiritual meaning of liberation.
Preserve the meaning of freedom from attachment rather than interpreting it as indifference or irresponsibility.
Preserve the meaning of mental equanimity and balance.
Preserve the philosophical meaning of ego or ego-identification.
Preserve the philosophical meaning of Prakriti where the source uses it in that sense.
Translate according to the philosophical context and do not automatically interpret it as simply 'man'.
Preserve the spiritual meaning of surrender to the Divine.
Translate according to context and preserve the meaning of deliberate intention or resolve.
Translate according to the source context and distinguish desire from ordinary preference where appropriate.
Translate directly according to the source context.
Preserve the distinction between mind and intellect where the source makes that distinction.
Preserve the philosophical distinction between buddhi and the ordinary mind.
Translate according to the spiritual/philosophical context.
Preserve the spiritual meaning of the witnessing consciousness.
Preserve the inner/spiritual sense of peace when that is the meaning in the source.
Preserve the meaning of psychological or emotional attachment according to context.
Translate according to whether the source means inner surrender or offering an action to the Divine.
Preserve the devotional meaning of grace from the Divine.
Translate according to the surrounding context and preserve the devotional meaning.
Use the source context to distinguish ordinary happiness from deeper spiritual bliss.
Translate according to context; do not automatically remove the spiritual meaning.
Translate directly while preserving the philosophical context provided by the source.
Preserve the spiritual/philosophical meaning rather than reducing it to general self-awareness.
Preserve the philosophical concept. If the target language commonly retains the Sanskrit term, it may be retained with an appropriate explanation only when the source itself provides one.
